bull_bear.body:
- "Disciplined Capital Allocation Guided by strong parentage" and a "Robust balance sheet with controlled leverage, even post acquisition" are the deck's stated principles; the MD frames it as "driving ambitious growth plan with capital allocation discipline".
- Early payment of Non-Convertible Debentures worth ₹423 crore in March 2026 through internal accruals, prior to maturity, following the maiden NCD issue in FY25 raised to fund the Arjas acquisition.
- Standalone gross debt to equity moved 0.19 / 0.11 / 0.06 / 0.40 / 0.11 across FY22-FY26; the consolidated series is shown as 0.19 / 0.11 / 0.06 / 0.72 / 0.31. Standalone net debt swung to a ₹819 crore increase (utilised mainly for financing the Arjas acquisition) and then a ₹583 crore decrease generated mainly through core SMIORE cash flows.
- Liquidity at Q1FY27: ₹534 crore standalone and ₹565 crore consolidated cash & cash equivalents; access to diversified funding through both banking channels and capital markets.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Occupational health & safety in a high-risk mining and smelting operation — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: given the high-risk nature of operations, failure to manage safety may result in workplace injuries, regulatory non-compliance, legal penalties and operational disruptions, while exposure to dust, heat and noise creates occupational health risks; incidents also affect workforce morale and reputation. Mitigated through Standard Operating Procedures conforming to ISO 45001:2018, regular training and mock drills, and regular safety audits and inspections.
- Governance, compliance and ethics failure — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: non-adherence to governance practices, non-compliance with applicable regulations or unethical business conduct may result in reputational damage, penalties and loss of stakeholder trust, affecting long-term performance. Mitigated via the Employees' Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, training and awareness sessions, a compliance monitoring system and periodic internal and external audits.
- Human rights and community/contract-labour relations — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: operations involve extensive engagement with employees, contract workers, local communities and other stakeholders, and failure to respect and uphold human rights may lead to regulatory actions, legal disputes, social unrest, operational delays and reputational damage. Mitigated through the POSH policy, a mechanism for raising concerns and resolving disputes, just and favourable working conditions and advocacy of gender equality.
- Commodity price / realisation volatility — FY26 was a muted year from a realisations standpoint, with prices across both manganese ore and iron ore bottoming out in Q2FY26 and Q3FY26; the year-to-date average spot price for 44% grade manganese ore from China was down 22% in October 2025 against the 2024 annual average, and the USGS-reported 62% Fe fines price averaged below the prior-year level. Realisations, not volumes, drove the softness in FY26 and remain outside the Company's control.
- Dependence on the global and domestic steel cycle — Roughly 96% of manganese ore consumption is directed into steelmaking, so demand closely follows steel output. Global crude steel output declined for a second consecutive year in 2025 (down 1.1% to 1.93 billion tonnes) on persistent Chinese property-sector weakness, and global finished steel consumption was unchanged, weighing directly on manganese and iron ore prices. A prolonged steel downcycle transmits straight into the Company's mining and ferroalloys segments.
- Geographic, asset and product concentration with no export offset — All mines are located at Deogiri, Subbarayanahalli, Kammathuru and Ramghad in Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karnataka, with a single plant at Vyasanakere, Mariyammanahalli, Hosapete, Vijayanagara District. The BRSR records no international plants, offices or markets and exports as Nil percent of total turnover, so the business is fully exposed to a single mining district and to domestic demand. Product mix is also concentrated: mining accounts for 76.22% of standalone turnover, with iron ore alone at 65.12%.
- Regulatory and approval dependence on mining limits, environmental consents and forest land — Output is capped by Maximum Permissible Annual Production limits, and expansion and evacuation infrastructure depend on approvals such as Consent for Operation and Consent for Operation - Expansion plus a Forest Lease Agreement executed with the Deputy Conservator of Forests for the DCS crossing 2.4314 hectares of forest land; the DCS itself is being set up in line with directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Any delay or adverse change in these approvals directly constrains volumes and project timelines. Regulatory change also hits costs — new Labour Codes notified by the Government of India gave rise to an exceptional item in FY26.
- Macro and geopolitical supply shock raising energy and input costs — The MD&A flags that downside risks dominate the outlook: the West Asia conflict is a negative supply shock, with the assumed oil price rising to about $82 per barrel in 2026, elevated energy, fertiliser and industrial input prices, a wholesale price index that rose from 2.1% in February to 3.9% in March 2026 signalling cost-push pressures, and adverse/severe scenarios in which global growth falls to 2.5% or 1.8% in 2026. A longer or broader conflict, deeper geopolitical fragmentation or renewed trade tensions could weaken growth and destabilise financial markets.

- In coke, run the business through conversion/contract manufacturing rather than merchant production: about 46% of Coke Oven capacity (two of four batteries) is secured under a conversion arrangement with a marquee customer from April 2025, removing pricing risk on contracted volumes, giving a steady production base and generating waste-heat energy; own merchant coke production kept deliberately low

- Diversify Arjas Steel beyond its traditional automotive market into forging, railways, defence and heavy engineering, while steadily building a non-automotive business pipeline; Arjas produces over 100 grades of SBQ and alloy steel and supplies a marquee set of automotive OEMs
- Maintain a strengthened balance sheet — acquisition borrowings substantially repaid from internal accruals and standalone net debt free status — to provide resilience and flexibility to fund the next phase of growth
- Balance reinvestment for growth with shareholder rewards (Bonus Issue in the ratio 2:1 during FY26 and a recommended final dividend)
- Actively evaluate further projects at both the standalone and the Arjas Steel levels, to be disclosed as and when approved by the Board; intent is to grow the group steadily and responsibly

The policy sets out the circumstances and factors the Board considers when deciding between distribution and retention of profits, and commits the Company to strike the right balance between the quantum of dividend paid and the amount of profits retained in the business, to maintain a consistent approach in dividend pay-out plans, and to facilitate a process of dividend recommendation, declaration and pay-out that ensures regular dividend income for shareholders alongside long-term capital appreciation for all stakeholders. outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SMIORE completed all its interim mining expansions in the previous year and FY26 was the first full year of operating at the enhanced Maximum Permissible Annual Production (MPAP) limits of 0.599 MTPA for manganese ore and 4.45 MTPA for iron ore, which delivered highest-ever production and sales in both ores. On a consolidated basis the group now runs four segments with installed capacity of 0.599 MTPA manganese ore and 4.45 MTPA iron ore in Mining, 95,000/1,25,000 TPA of ferroalloys (SiMn/FeMn), 0.50 MTPA of coke with 32 MW of Waste-Heat Recovery Boiler based power, and 0.585 MTPA of steel manufacturing with 21 MW of waste-heat based captive power added through the acquisition of material subsidiary Arjas Steel Private Limited and step-down subsidiary Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited. Two named projects are in flight. First, a 300 tonne-per-hour, 1.2 km Downhill Conveyor Pipe System (DCS) from the Kammathuru iron ore mine to the PMBR railway siding: the proposal is completed, necessary approvals including Consent for Operation - Expansion were obtained during the year, a Forest Lease Agreement was executed with the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Government of Karnataka, Ballari Division, and the system is expected to be operational within H1FY27; it passes through 2.4314 hectares of forest land in the Deogiri Swamimalai Forest Block and is intended to enable environment-friendly ore transportation and fetch better realisations by delivering ore directly to the railway siding, with SMIORE the first private mine in Ballari and Vijayanagara districts to comply with a DCS for ore evacuation in line with Supreme Court directions. Second, a 2.0 MTPA Beneficiation Plant at Deogiri is in the process of being set up to upgrade iron ore grade concentrate suitable for pellet manufacturing, designed to deliver 1.0 to 1.2 MTPA of output using crushing, screening, grinding, magnetic separation and filtration, with the aim of improved realisation through pellet feed quality and reduced waste. Beyond capacity, the Company received Consent for Operation approval on one mining lease to handle incidental iron ore of 0.327 MT by 30 August 2026, permitting sale of already-excavated ore over and above annual production limits. In coke, roughly 46% of Coke Oven capacity (2 of 4 batteries) is committed under a contract manufacturing agreement continued into FY27, and the Company is actively engaging additional customers to recommence the remaining 2 batteries, which would raise utilisation and waste-heat energy generation and in turn support better ferroalloys capacity utilisation in FY27. Captive power is held through SPVs — ReNew Sandur Green Energy Private Limited with 42.9 MW of solar-wind hybrid capacity for ferroalloys and Amplus Arjas Solar Private Limited with 20.4 MW of solar capacity for steel — and the Company had entered into a Share Subscription and Shareholders' Agreement with ReNew Green Energy Solutions (the description of which is truncated in the source text).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Ore realisations eased through much of FY26, but domestic benchmarks firmed up towards the close of the year, giving the Company a better footing as it begins FY27
- Closing stock of iron ore carried into FY27 gives a ready surplus to sell early in the new year
- Ferroalloys market conditions stayed challenging for much of FY26, but management is encouraged by early signs of recovery in the broader iron and steel industry, which should support volumes and realisations in the coming year
- Waste-heat energy generated from the contracted coke oven batteries feeds directly into powering ferroalloys, linking coke utilisation to ferroalloys output
- Manganese ore sales gathered pace as the year progressed, in both external markets and captive consumption at the ferroalloys plant, where the Company is steadily absorbing more of its own ore
- A Government of India quantitative restriction on coking-coal imports, extended through 31 December 2025, supported the domestic coking-coal market during the year
- India's steel sector advancing toward its 300 MT capacity goal underpins domestic iron ore demand; India also remains a significant net importer of manganese ore, underscoring the demand-supply gap and anticipated acceleration in manganese demand
- Manganese has no satisfactory substitute in its major applications and roughly 96% of manganese ore consumption is directed into steelmaking, so demand tracks steel output; battery demand (high-purity manganese, LMO chemistry) is emerging but remains a small share
- Ferroalloy demand is anchored to the steel industry, particularly Asia-Pacific, supported by rising demand for high-strength low-alloy steels across automotive, construction, machinery and energy, and by infrastructure and urbanisation spending in China and India
- Soft global backdrop: global crude steel output declined for a second consecutive year in 2025 on Chinese property-sector weakness, weighing on manganese and iron ore prices, even as India sustained double-digit growth in crude steel production
- Iron ore market structurally shifted toward lower-grade 61% Fe-based pricing, with Chinese import curbs driving trade realignment and slower-than-announced Simandou ramp-up (about 15-20 MT of exports projected in 2026) expected to keep prices resilient in the first half of 2026
- The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entering its definitive period in January 2026 adds a further regulatory dimension for producers
- India enters FY27 at the intersection of domestic resilience and external turbulence; the IMF raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.5%, supported by carry-over momentum from FY26, a reduction in United States tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 10%, and resilient domestic demand, while the West Asia conflict represents a supply shock to energy and industrial input prices
- A conversion arrangement with a marquee customer secured about 46% of Coke Oven capacity from April 2025, equivalent to two of four batteries operating round-the-clock, and the same capacity has been contracted again for FY27
- The Company is in discussions with additional customers to restart the remaining two Coke Oven batteries
- Arjas Steel supplies a marquee set of automotive OEMs and is steadily building a non-automotive business pipeline

FY26 was a muted year from a realisations standpoint, with prices across both manganese ore and iron ore bottoming out in Q2FY26 and Q3FY26; the year-to-date average spot price for 44% grade manganese ore from China was down 22% in October 2025 against the 2024 annual average, and the USGS-reported 62% Fe fines price averaged below the prior-year level. Realisations, not volumes, drove the softness in FY26 and remain outside the Company's control.

Roughly 96% of manganese ore consumption is directed into steelmaking, so demand closely follows steel output. Global crude steel output declined for a second consecutive year in 2025 (down 1.1% to 1.93 billion tonnes) on persistent Chinese property-sector weakness, and global finished steel consumption was unchanged, weighing directly on manganese and iron ore prices. A prolonged steel downcycle transmits straight into the Company's mining and ferroalloys segments.
risks.risk: Dependence on the global and domestic steel cycle

The BRSR records no international plants, offices or markets and exports as Nil percent of total turnover, so the business is fully exposed to a single mining district and to domestic demand. risks.risk: Regulatory and approval dependence on mining limits, environmental consents and forest land

risks.risk: Occupational health & safety in a high-risk mining and smelting operation
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: given the high-risk nature of operations, failure to manage safety may result in workplace injuries, regulatory non-compliance, legal penalties and operational disruptions, while exposure to dust, heat and noise creates occupational health risks; incidents also affect workforce morale and reputation. Mitigated through Standard Operating Procedures conforming to ISO 45001:2018, regular training and mock drills, and regular safety audits and inspections.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: non-adherence to governance practices, non-compliance with applicable regulations or unethical business conduct may result in reputational damage, penalties and loss of stakeholder trust, affecting long-term performance. Mitigated via the Employees' Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, training and awareness sessions, a compliance monitoring system and periodic internal and external audits.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: operations involve extensive engagement with employees, contract workers, local communities and other stakeholders, and failure to respect and uphold human rights may lead to regulatory actions, legal disputes, social unrest, operational delays and reputational damage. Mitigated through the POSH policy, a mechanism for raising concerns and resolving disputes, just and favourable working conditions and advocacy of gender equality.

FY26 was a muted year from a realisations standpoint, with prices across both manganese ore and iron ore bottoming out in Q2FY26 and Q3FY26; the year-to-date average spot price for 44% grade manganese ore from China was down 22% in October 2025 against the 2024 annual average, and the USGS-reported 62% Fe fines price averaged below the prior-year level. Realisations, not volumes, drove the softness in FY26 and remain outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Dependence on the global and domestic steel cycle
risks.note: Roughly 96% of manganese ore consumption is directed into steelmaking, so demand closely follows steel output. Global crude steel output declined for a second consecutive year in 2025 (down 1.1% to 1.93 billion tonnes) on persistent Chinese property-sector weakness, and global finished steel consumption was unchanged, weighing directly on manganese and iron ore prices. A prolonged steel downcycle transmits straight into the Company's mining and ferroalloys segments.

risks.risk: Geographic, asset and product concentration with no export offset
risks.note: All mines are located at Deogiri, Subbarayanahalli, Kammathuru and Ramghad in Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karnataka, with a single plant at Vyasanakere, Mariyammanahalli, Hosapete, Vijayanagara District. The BRSR records no international plants, offices or markets and exports as Nil percent of total turnover, so the business is fully exposed to a single mining district and to domestic demand. Product mix is also concentrated: mining accounts for 76.22% of standalone turnover, with iron ore alone at 65.12%.

risks.risk: Regulatory and approval dependence on mining limits, environmental consents and forest land
risks.note: Output is capped by Maximum Permissible Annual Production limits, and expansion and evacuation infrastructure depend on approvals such as Consent for Operation and Consent for Operation - Expansion plus a Forest Lease Agreement executed with the Deputy Conservator of Forests for the DCS crossing 2.4314 hectares of forest land; the DCS itself is being set up in line with directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Any delay or adverse change in these approvals directly constrains volumes and project timelines. Regulatory change also hits costs — new Labour Codes notified by the Government of India gave rise to an exceptional item in FY26.

risks.risk: Macro and geopolitical supply shock raising energy and input costs
risks.note: The MD&A flags that downside risks dominate the outlook: the West Asia conflict is a negative supply shock, with the assumed oil price rising to about $82 per barrel in 2026, elevated energy, fertiliser and industrial input prices, a wholesale price index that rose from 2.1% in February to 3.9% in March 2026 signalling cost-push pressures, and adverse/severe scenarios in which global growth falls to 2.5% or 1.8% in 2026. A longer or broader conflict, deeper geopolitical fragmentation or renewed trade tensions could weaken growth and destabilise financial markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: The Sandur Manganese & Iron Ores Limited (SMIORE) is one of India's leading private sector miners and commodity producers — the 2nd largest manganese ore miner in India, the 3rd largest iron ore miner in Karnataka, and, through its subsidiary Arjas Steel, among the top 5 players in the SBQ steel …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: SMIORE mines and sells manganese ore and iron ore from leases in Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karnataka, and upgrades part of that ore into ferroalloys (silicomanganese/ferromanganese) at its Vyasanakere plant, alongside a coke & energy business now run largely under contract manufacturing arrangements. Following the acquisition of material subsidiary Arjas Steel Private Limited and step-down subsidiary Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited, the group also manufactures special bar quality (SBQ)/alloy steel. It operates on a Business-to-Business basis, serving industrial customers — principally steel manufacturers and ferroalloy producers — with captive solar/wind and waste-heat power assets held through separate SPVs supporting the ferroalloys and steel segments.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Ore realisations eased through much of FY26, but domestic benchmarks firmed up towards the close of the year, giving the Company a better footing as it begins FY27
- Closing stock of iron ore carried into FY27 gives a ready surplus to sell early in the new year
- Ferroalloys market conditions stayed challenging for much of FY26, but management is encouraged by early signs of recovery in the broader iron and steel industry, which should support volumes and realisations in the coming year
- Waste-heat energy generated from the contracted coke oven batteries feeds directly into powering ferroalloys, linking coke utilisation to ferroalloys output
- Manganese ore sales gathered pace as the year progressed, in both external markets and captive consumption at the ferroalloys plant, where the Company is steadily absorbing more of its own ore
- A Government of India quantitative restriction on coking-coal imports, extended through 31 December 2025, supported the domestic coking-coal market during the year
- India's steel sector advancing toward its 300 MT capacity goal underpins domestic iron ore demand; India also remains a significant net importer of manganese ore, underscoring the demand-supply gap and anticipated acceleration in manganese demand
- Manganese has no satisfactory substitute in its major applications and roughly 96% of manganese ore consumption is directed into steelmaking, so demand tracks steel output; battery demand (high-purity manganese, LMO chemistry) is emerging but remains a small share
- Ferroalloy demand is anchored to the steel industry, particularly Asia-Pacific, supported by rising demand for high-strength low-alloy steels across automotive, construction, machinery and energy, and by infrastructure and urbanisation spending in China and India
- Soft global backdrop: global crude steel output declined for a second consecutive year in 2025 on Chinese property-sector weakness, weighing on manganese and iron ore prices, even as India sustained double-digit growth in crude steel production
- Iron ore market structurally shifted toward lower-grade 61% Fe-based pricing, with Chinese import curbs driving trade realignment and slower-than-announced Simandou ramp-up (about 15-20 MT of exports projected in 2026) expected to keep prices resilient in the first half of 2026
- The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entering its definitive period in January 2026 adds a further regulatory dimension for producers
- India enters FY27 at the intersection of domestic resilience and external turbulence; the IMF raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.5%, supported by carry-over momentum from FY26, a reduction in United States tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 10%, and resilient domestic demand, while the West Asia conflict represents a supply shock to energy and industrial input prices
- A conversion arrangement with a marquee customer secured about 46% of Coke Oven capacity from April 2025, equivalent to two of four batteries operating round-the-clock, and the same capacity has been contracted again for FY27
- The Company is in discussions with additional customers to restart the remaining two Coke Oven batteries
- Arjas Steel supplies a marquee set of automotive OEMs and is steadily building a non-automotive business pipeline

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SMIORE completed all its interim mining expansions in the previous year and FY26 was the first full year of operating at the enhanced Maximum Permissible Annual Production (MPAP) limits of 0.599 MTPA for manganese ore and 4.45 MTPA for iron ore, which delivered highest-ever production and sales in both ores. On a consolidated basis the group now runs four segments with installed capacity of 0.599 MTPA manganese ore and 4.45 MTPA iron ore in Mining, 95,000/1,25,000 TPA of ferroalloys (SiMn/FeMn), 0.50 MTPA of coke with 32 MW of Waste-Heat Recovery Boiler based power, and 0.585 MTPA of steel manufacturing with 21 MW of waste-heat based captive power added through the acquisition of material subsidiary Arjas Steel Private Limited and step-down subsidiary Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited. Two named projects are in flight. First, a 300 tonne-per-hour, 1.2 km Downhill Conveyor Pipe System (DCS) from the Kammathuru iron ore mine to the PMBR railway siding: the proposal is completed, necessary approvals including Consent for Operation - Expansion were obtained during the year, a Forest Lease Agreement was executed with the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Government of Karnataka, Ballari Division, and the system is expected to be operational within H1FY27; it passes through 2.4314 hectares of forest land in the Deogiri Swamimalai Forest Block and is intended to enable environment-friendly ore transportation and fetch better realisations by delivering ore directly to the railway siding, with SMIORE the first private mine in Ballari and Vijayanagara districts to comply with a DCS for ore evacuation in line with Supreme Court directions. Second, a 2.0 MTPA Beneficiation Plant at Deogiri is in the process of being set up to upgrade iron ore grade concentrate suitable for pellet manufacturing, designed to deliver 1.0 to 1.2 MTPA of output using crushing, screening, grinding, magnetic separation and filtration, with the aim of improved realisation through pellet feed quality and reduced waste. Beyond capacity, the Company received Consent for Operation approval on one mining lease to handle incidental iron ore of 0.327 MT by 30 August 2026, permitting sale of already-excavated ore over and above annual production limits. In coke, roughly 46% of Coke Oven capacity (2 of 4 batteries) is committed under a contract manufacturing agreement continued into FY27, and the Company is actively engaging additional customers to recommence the remaining 2 batteries, which would raise utilisation and waste-heat energy generation and in turn support better ferroalloys capacity utilisation in FY27. Captive power is held through SPVs — ReNew Sandur Green Energy Private Limited with 42.9 MW of solar-wind hybrid capacity for ferroalloys and Amplus Arjas Solar Private Limited with 20.4 MW of solar capacity for steel — and the Company had entered into a Share Subscription and Shareholders' Agreement with ReNew Green Energy Solutions (the description of which is truncated in the source text).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale and rank in a scarce resource: 2nd largest manganese ore miner in India and 3rd largest iron ore miner in Karnataka, with over 7 decades of operating history
- Integration across the value chain — mining, ferroalloys, coke & energy and, post-acquisition, steel — allowing captive consumption of own ore (0.61 LT of manganese ore consumed captively in FY26)
- Captive and green power through SPVs: 42.9 MW solar-wind hybrid (ReNew Sandur Green Energy) for ferroalloys and 20.4 MW solar (Amplus Arjas Solar) for steel, plus waste-heat recovery based power
- Environmental/regulatory standing — the 7-Star SDF rating and a decade of 5-Star ratings; first private mine in Ballari and Vijayanagara districts to comply with setting up a Downhill Conveyor System for ore evacuation in line with Supreme Court directions
- Balance-sheet strength: prepaid and redeemed Non-Convertible Debentures ahead of maturity and achieved standalone net debt-free status as of 31 March 2026
- Risk insulation via contract manufacturing in coke — shifting from own coke production to conversion agreements insulates the Company from international coking coal price and exchange-rate volatility
- Mining expansions completed and fully compliant with the parameters prescribed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, with MPAP limits now fully operational

other.body:

- [New ventures] Incorporation initiated of Royal Sandur Hospitality Private Limited and Royal Sandur Academy Private Limited, and the company is evaluating an opportunity in medical devices, consumables and manufacturing.

themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining.
